issues.legal_issue: A revisional court may interfere with an appellate authority’s findings of fact when those findings are improper and illegal.
material_facts: The trial court found that the premises had been let for residential use and that the tenant had changed their use.
The appellate authority reversed that finding, concluding that the premises had been let for running a printing press.
In revision, the High Court reversed the appellate authority’s findings.
issues.conclusion: The High Court acted within its jurisdiction under Section 15(5) by reversing findings of fact that were improper and illegal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15(5) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restrictions Act, 1949 permits the High Court, in revision, to reverse factual findings when they are improper and illegal. The judgment refers to Faqir Chand v. R.R. Bhanot; Shalimar Tar Products Ltd. v. H.C. Sharma; Duli Chand (dead) by L.Rs. v. Jagmender Dass; Hari Mittal v. B.M. Sikka; Ram Dass v. Ishwar Chander; Vinod Kumar Arora v. Smt. Surjit Kaur; M/s. New Garage Ltd. v. Khushwant Singh; Kamal Arora v. Amar Singh; and Ved Parkash v. Darshan Lal Jain.

predicates.rent_control_revision_proceeding: The matter is a revision in a rent-control proceeding.
predicates.factual_findings_are_improper: The revisional court finds that the appellate authority’s factual findings are improper.
predicates.factual_findings_are_illegal: The revisional court finds that the appellate authority’s factual findings are illegal.
predicates.revisional_court_may_reverse_factual_fin: The revisional court may reverse the appellate authority’s factual findings.

issues.definition: When a rent-control revision presents appellate factual findings that are both improper and illegal, the revisional court may reverse them.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant is liable for eviction for changing the use of premises let to that tenant for residential purposes when the tenant uses them for a different purpose.
material_facts: The rent note was signed by the tenant in his own name and stipulated that the premises were to be used for residential purposes.
The tenant was the sole proprietor of the business operating a printing press in the premises.
The High Court found that the premises had been let to the tenant, not to the business, and that the tenant had used them for a purpose other than the one for which they were let.
issues.conclusion: The premises were let to the tenant for residential use, and the High Court’s decision that the tenant was liable for eviction for changing their use was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 11 and 15 of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restrictions Act, 1949, the decision turned on the purpose for which the premises were let and whether the tenant used them for another purpose. The court concluded from the tenant’s personal execution of the rent note and his sole proprietorship of the business that the lease was to him for residence. The judgment refers to Faqir Chand v. R.R. Bhanot; Shalimar Tar Products Ltd. v. H.C. Sharma; Duli Chand (dead) by L.Rs. v. Jagmender Dass; Hari Mittal v. B.M. Sikka; Ram Dass v. Ishwar Chander; Vinod Kumar Arora v. Smt. Surjit Kaur; M/s. New Garage Ltd. v. Khushwant Singh; Kamal Arora v. Amar Singh; and Ved Parkash v. Darshan Lal Jain.

rule.if: change_of_user_eviction_proceeding and lease_personally_signed_by_tenant and lease_restricted_to_residential_use and tenant_is_sole_proprietor_of_business_operating_there

predicates.change_of_user_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks eviction on the ground that the tenant changed the use of the premises.
predicates.lease_personally_signed_by_tenant: The tenant personally signed the lease or rent note.
predicates.lease_restricted_to_residential_use: The lease or rent note specified that the premises were to be used for residence.
predicates.tenant_is_sole_proprietor_of_business_op: The tenant was the sole proprietor of the business operating in the premises.
predicates.tenant_is_liable_for_eviction_for_change: The tenant is liable for eviction because the premises were used for a purpose other than the one for which they were let.

issues.definition: When a change-of-user eviction proceeding concerns a personally signed residential lease and the tenant is the sole proprietor of a business operating there, the tenant is liable for eviction for the different use.
